To prove the accessibility of employing linear regression based on fewer selected data input, Fig. 7.7a shows an accuracy comparison based on more than 100 prediction outputs. Note that instead of only inputting all these 20 selected parameters, we have also randomly chosen 10 parameters out of those 20 parameters. Among all the Neural Network predicted output, an overall less than 5% error is achieved. A similar prediction accuracy is observed using 20-parameter- linear-regression algorithm. However, the threshold errors largely increase due to the lack of input datapoints we use to feed the algorithm. Some Linear regression predicted values examples are further illustrated in Fig. 7.7b. As a comparison, with further fewer input data points (10 input), we find a slight decrease in overall prediction accuracy by 3 to 5 percent, however still capable as an efficient approach to investigate the weights of each parameter. To further illustrate the contrast, we plot out the predicted Voc, Jsc and FF value based on ANN and LR shown in Fig. 7.8. As the comparison to the ground truth value, ANN tends to have a better sparsity prediction which makes the error distribution in Fig. 6a smaller than LR correspondingly. Figure 7.8. A Voc, Jsc, and FF comparison of 250 predicted value distributions based on Neural Network algorithm (NN), Linear regression (LR) and their ground truth values. As linear regression tries to find a possible linear relationship between the input parameters with our desired output Voc, Jsc and FF values, it is important to determine if linear regression is the only possible relationship in linking the algorithm with the physical meanings. Thus, polynomial regression is carried out, which finds the possible nonlinearities between the inputs and the outputs. We compared the LR and PR trained fitting r2 value for relationship between the training dataset and the ground truth output. In general, polynomial regression has an almost perfect trained r2 value (over 0.9), meaning a perfect learning fitting accuracy as shown in Fig. 7.9a for both Voc, Jsc and FF.
